audit.title: Feed Types

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong for a hub: opens with "Chainlink Data Feeds provide multiple feed types for different onchain use cases," then a self-contained table. Each row stands alone. No dangling cross-references.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: The comparison table is the right structure for extraction; measured facts confirm one clean table, zero level skips. Weakness: single 171-word section with no H2s means the whole page is one chunk — fine at this size, but no per-feed-type anchors for granular retrieval.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 0 numerals, 0 units, no version or network details. A hub page needn't carry latencies, but naming e.g. supported chains or update model per type would add liftable specifics.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 7 internal links to the canonical per-type pages, appropriate for a hub. No external/primary sources, but none are expected here; the internal linking is the correct pattern.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good: each purpose cell is a crisp, verbatim-liftable clause (e.g. SmartData as "RWA-focused single-value and multi-variable (MVR) feeds"). A missing top-level definition of "Data Feed" itself is the gap.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension: JSON-LD absent, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, head metadata not captured. This is the highest-confidence defect on the page.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable; an index page needs no code. Scored neutral, no action needed.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what types exist" well; does not cover "which feed type do I use for lending / for RWAs / for MEV" as explicit selectable text. Adding decision guidance would capture selection-intent queries.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent entity naming ("Chainlink Labs–managed," "SmartData," "SVR"), no jargon left undefined. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a thin navigation hub: one H1, one intro line, and a six-row comparison table routing to each Chainlink Data Feed type. Its biggest strength is a clean, liftable table where each feed type carries a crisp one-line purpose definition — ideal for an engine answering "what feed types does Chainlink offer." Its biggest weakness is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates, so agents get zero structured trust signals. The honest verdict: content is fine for its narrow job, but as an index it under-serves selection-intent queries ("which feed type should I use for X") and carries no metadata scaffolding — Developing, not because the prose is weak but because the page is minimal and metadata-bare.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-sentence definition of a Chainlink Data Feed
recommendations.issue: "Chainlink Data Feeds provide multiple feed types for different onchain use cases."
recommendations.change: Precede/expand with a liftable definition, e.g. "A Chainlink Data Feed is an onchain contract that delivers decentralized, aggregated offchain data (such as asset prices) to smart contracts. Chainlink offers six feed types:" — then the table.
recommendations.why: gives engines a self-contained definition to quote when answering "what is a Chainlink Data Feed," instead of falling back to generic priors.

recommendations.title: Add selection-intent guidance ("which feed type should I use")
recommendations.issue: page answers "what types exist" but not "which to pick."
recommendations.change: add a short "When to use which" decision list mapping use case → feed type (e.g. "Lending/collateral → Price Feeds; Tokenized RWA reserves/NAV → SmartData; MEV recapture → SVR Feeds; L2 dApps needing liveness checks → L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds").
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by use case, not by product name; this captures retrieval that the concept-titled table misses.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata: canonical URL, JSON-LD `TechArticle`/`CollectionPage`, last-updated
recommendations.issue: canonical MISSING, 0 JSON-LD blocks, no dateModified (measured facts).
recommendations.change: emit a canonical link to the non-`.md` URL, a JSON-LD block typed appropriately with `about` entries for each feed type, and a visible last-updated date.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust; verify by passing raw `<head>` to the CLI.

recommendations.title: Give each feed type an anchor for granular retrieval
recommendations.issue: entire page is a single retrievable chunk with no per-type sections.
recommendations.change: optionally add short H2 subsections (or ensure the linked detail pages carry answer-first leads); at minimum keep the one-line definitions crisp so each row survives chunking.
recommendations.why: improves the odds an engine lifts the exact feed type relevant to a narrow query.

recommendations.title: Add one or two concrete specifics per feed type
recommendations.where: table cells or a follow-on line
recommendations.change: where accurate and stable, note e.g. supported network families or the update mechanism per type; avoid figures that go stale.
recommendations.why: quantitative/specific claims measurably raise citation rate; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

antiPatterns: Stale/undated content risk: no visible last-updated or version signal (measured: dateModified absent).
Otherwise none — no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references, no ambiguous entities.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced inline — good; confirm it enumerates this page and its child feed-type pages.
Canonical/JSON-LD emission is likely a site-template concern; fixing it here should be handled at the docs-platform level so all hub pages benefit.
Ensure the six linked detail pages each open answer-first, since this hub's citation value depends on the pages it routes to being retrievable.
